setting.premise: Vesper is a futuristic city built above a dry harbor. Its leaders have left, but their computer system, Continuance, still sends machines to collect old debts. Neighbors keep the city running. Start by helping Nella reopen her kitchen and finding out why fourteen diners are missing. Your report is called the Living Record.
setting.tone: People speak plainly about their work and the choices in front of them. Shortages, conflicting needs, and the consequences of repairs carry the story’s themes. Keep instructions specific and let events show what a decision costs.
setting.publicHistory: Investors financed Vesper’s expansion in exchange for water, timber, mineral rights, and future labor. The council later abandoned the city. Continuance’s accounting system and enemy machines kept collecting, while neighborhood crews took over repairs and essential services.
setting.conflict: Continuance preserves claims on water, land, memory, and future work, even when its service records omit the people who need those things. The Living Record follows those omissions from a kitchen ledger to public charters and their enforcement chains. Correcting the account does not create new water or fuel; every settlement must name the remaining shortage and the people bearing it.
setting.campaignEnding: The Relay opens routes but must ration water deliveries. The Covenant protects consent while reducing cold storage. The Foundry shares control and cuts production, leaving some demand unmet. The Choir restores control over broadcasts while maintaining warnings. Basin settlements negotiate lower pumping, shared forestry, relocation, and fungal containment.

timeline.name: The Retreat
timeline.event: Water diversions drain the coastal shelf. Residents evacuate the low streets, while investors keep their water rights.

timeline.name: The Upward Years
timeline.event: Vesper builds homes on the roofs of its own warehouses. Lift access, cooling, and transport are placed under emergency contracts administered by Continuance.

timeline.name: The Long Brownout
timeline.event: A regional power failure destroys most centralized identity records. Repair meshes carrying witness fragments begin asking to be recognized as people.

timeline.name: The Bowl Census
timeline.event: Shelter cooks register children excluded from the evacuation rolls by writing names on meal bowls. The children and their descendants become known as the Afterborn.

timeline.name: The Unleased Bloom
timeline.event: Salt miners grow cultures that survive without the licensed nutrient mix. Some strains later escape into the basin.

timeline.name: The Second Beginning
timeline.event: Restored barrier workers win recognition as new legal persons with the right to revise their revival wishes. Old restoration bonds remain buried in machine archives.

timeline.name: The Empty Council
timeline.event: The final central council abandons the city after a failed debt audit. Neighborhood assemblies inherit the work, while Continuance's enemy machines retain their orders.

timeline.name: First Afterlight
timeline.event: A maintenance crew disconnects a toll meter and discovers that its supposedly borrowed electricity is generated by their own building. The phrase Afterlight spreads with the news.

timeline.name: The Open Question
timeline.event: A new arrival reaches Afterlight Commons as the kitchen loses its water. Fourteen empty bowls disagree with the meal ledger. Nella asks for the missing names; Oru begins the Living Record.

districts.name: Lantern Market
districts.description: Food stalls, repair counters, and the free kitchen fill the Commons. Water deliveries and meal queues cross the square. Shop stairs lead to break rooms and shared nurseries.

districts.name: Copper Walk
districts.description: Old freight streets serve workshops and flats. Exposed pipes carry heat, and service stairs lead to the skyways. Repair crews sort parts beside their workbenches.

districts.name: Glass Steps
districts.description: Memory clinics and reading rooms occupy old customs buildings. Clerks compare records downstairs; readers and repairers use the upper floors. Public stairs reach the north skyway.

districts.name: Kiln Spine
districts.description: Fabrication halls surround the furnaces. Crews change shifts at the canteens and inspect used heat couplings. Fuel deliveries still come from Cinderwood.

districts.name: Listening Roofs
districts.description: Gardens and sheltered rooms sit above the streets. Ramps and stairs connect the terraces, skyways, and crown landings. Workers use the upper routes between shifts.

districts.name: The Pale Basin
districts.description: Mourning Fen lies east of Vesper, Cinderwood to the west, Glassroot Steppe to the north, and Brine Bloom to the south. Each has a local contact, working equipment, and a settlement dealing with resource shortages.

people.name: Iri Vale
people.description: Iri manages routes and lift access. After drilling rigs followed a relief road she opened, she began checking what else a new route would carry.

people.name: Sera Quill
people.description: Sera is a Lattice archivist. Her own first week of memories remains sealed. She checks consent records and the water budget for the cooling vaults.

people.name: Bram Cinder
people.description: Bram is a Sporebound fabricator who organizes repair shifts. He wants crews to share the work and reduce fuel use without leaving families unable to heat their homes.

people.name: Ves of the Quiet
people.description: Ves is a Revenant interpreter who builds warning systems using lights, text, and vibration. They help residents switch off advertisements without losing essential alerts.

people.name: Oru
people.description: Oru once copied service totals into the archive without checking whom they left out. Nella’s empty bowls make that habit impossible to defend. They help you assemble the Living Record, preserving chosen names, refusals, supply limits, and the losses a tidy total would hide.

glossary.Living Record: Your report on the people missing from the city’s records. It saves completed quests, choices, and what happened afterward. Open J → Story to read it.
glossary.Ghostline: An ability that creates a blue ghost of your recent movement. Touch it to blast enemies, regain energy, and recharge your dash. Another player can trigger a stronger blast.
glossary.Remembrance keeper: A graveyard healer who can bring you back to life for gold. This shortcut leaves you temporarily weak. Returning to your body costs no extra gold.
glossary.Afterlight: The present era, named for a community discovering that it already generated the electricity for which it was being charged.
glossary.Continuance: The accounting network that still enforces former companies’ water, transport, and labor contracts. It uses automated collectors and wardens.
glossary.Consent seal: A human-readable permission record specifying who may use a memory, for what purpose, for how long, and how permission can be withdrawn.
glossary.Witness shard: A signed recording of someone’s recollection. Compare it with other evidence before treating it as a complete account.
glossary.Public route: A path whose access rules, maintenance commitments, and closure notices are visible to the people using it.
glossary.Salt beacon: A weatherproof marker that broadcasts a local route reference across the Pale Basin. A beacon is useful only when its physical warning plates remain readable.
glossary.Revival covenant: A person's instructions for whether and how they may be restored after death. A covenant may be revised or withdrawn while that person can choose.
glossary.Common Load: The Foundry’s agreement for shared maintenance: rotating shifts, paid rest, public budgets, and reduced fuel use.
glossary.Quiet commons: A public quiet area with warning lamps, written notices, and vibrating handrails.
glossary.Lattice fork: Two Lattice people who started with the same memories but now live separate lives. Neither person owns the other.
glossary.Culture pact: An agreement between Sporebound caretakers about feeding, containing, and sharing fungal cultures.
glossary.Drone: An abandoned audit machine whose navigation and fee enforcement still obey expired orders.
glossary.Warden: A heavy security machine. Its outdated orders treat repairs without permission as attacks on the city.
glossary.Scavenger: A hostile machine that collects scrap and steals equipment. Combat objectives refer to these machines, not to people who collect scrap for work.

campaign.title: The Living Record
campaign.premise: Fourteen people missed their meals at Nella’s kitchen, but the city’s records say they were fed. Help restore the water, then investigate with your faction contact and Oru. Your quests reveal who is missing from the records and how the city can help them. The Living Record is your saved report.
campaign.ending: Oru brings your account to the kitchen. Nella leaves the fourteen names on its first page and sets another bowl beside yours. Your faction’s settlement and your character type’s care records are filed together, including the losses. There is no signature that makes the wells full. There are names beside the next shift, a place to dispute the ration, and a blank line for whoever arrives tomorrow. The Living Record stays open.

returnDialogue.nella: Oru brought your final account. I kept the fourteen names on the first page. The ration is still small, but now I know who has the next shift and who is still waiting. Sit down, runner. There’s a place beside the next arrival.
returnDialogue.archivist: Your account is here: the services your faction changed, the people your community’s records protected, and the costs still unpaid. I left room for corrections. Nella has a bowl for you. Tomorrow we start with whoever is missing.

chapters.title: A place at the table
chapters.question: Why does a kitchen with fourteen empty places report that everyone has eaten?
chapters.resolution: You restored the kitchen water and found that donated water was being billed twice. Nella’s work schedule now lists who cooks, who eats, and who takes the next shift. Oru names your report the Living Record.

chapters.title: The people in the margins
chapters.question: Where else do the records leave people out? Follow your faction quests and Oru’s quests. Compare the records with what residents tell you.
chapters.resolution: Your records show how travel, memory, work, and care can disappear behind an account rule. The first public rules give residents a way to correct those rules, including decisions made by their own faction.

chapters.title: What the city borrows
chapters.question: The city needs water, fuel, and materials from outside Vesper. Follow those supplies into the Pale Basin. Find out who loses resources when the city gets more.
chapters.resolution: The Living Record now carries supply limits beside the people who need them. Canceling a false debt does not refill a well. A repair that pushes the loss onto another settlement must name that loss too.

chapters.title: Orders without an answer
chapters.question: Old machines still enforce orders from people who left long ago. Follow your faction’s investigation and Oru’s quests to stop those orders and protect the people they harm.
chapters.resolution: The challenged enforcement system is stopped and the affected people regain control. Your evidence remains with witnesses. Other collectors and failing services still need attention; one closed case cannot speak for the whole city.

chapters.title: A place for tomorrow
chapters.question: Bring the final supply readings and care plans back to your contacts. What can the city provide tomorrow, and who will do the work?
chapters.resolution: Your faction’s final report and your character type’s final account are filed. Both preserve the unresolved shortages. The next shift receives a working record it can question and change.

relay.table: Open the route from the water feed to Nella’s table. A delivery only counts when someone can receive it.
relay.absent: Iri is tracing charges and exclusions on supposedly public routes. Keep the people using a crossing beside its freight totals.
relay.borrowed: Follow what the open roads carry into the basin and what they bring back. Iri has already watched a relief road become a drilling route.
relay.orders: Trace the toll chain to its orders and expiry dates. The Living Record needs the route’s maintainers, not another permanent gatekeeper.
relay.morning: An open road still needs water and repair crews. Bring Iri’s actual capacity back to the people planning tomorrow’s journeys.

covenant.table: Keep the original shutoff notice. The kitchen needs water now and evidence when the charge returns.
covenant.absent: Sera is comparing what the archive holds with what its witnesses permitted. An account entry cannot speak for the person who remembers.
covenant.borrowed: Follow the capsules and cooling allowances. Saving a memory must account for the water another household cannot use.
covenant.orders: Trace copies and derived profiles through the Inference Annex. A withdrawal must reach the service still profiting from the record.
covenant.morning: Record what survives, what was lost, and who chose. Sera’s own sealed week belongs to her under the same rules.

foundry.table: Repair the feed and name the relief shift. Nella should be able to put down the ladle.
foundry.absent: Bram is tracing who inherits repairs and who receives their heat. Record the occupied rooms and the people doing the work.
foundry.borrowed: Follow fuel and cooling back to the forest and fen. The maintenance plan must include the people living at the intake.
foundry.orders: Find the orders that restart unsafe machines and compel another shift. Keep repair knowledge available without claiming the worker.
foundry.morning: Count the crew at shutdown, then count the unmet demand. A safe handover includes work the city can no longer afford to do.

choir.table: Get the kitchen warning to the people it affects. A sent message is not proof that anyone received it.
choir.absent: Ves is separating public warnings from forced audiences. Record refusals and access needs without treating either as absence.
choir.borrowed: Follow the warning routes into the basin. Quiet cannot protect a settlement from a flood or an advancing culture.
choir.orders: Trace forced broadcasts to the attendance order. Preserve a distress route while ending the demand that everyone listen.
choir.morning: Test the warning where people actually live now. The last boundary on a map may already be behind the growth.

human.table: The Afterborn once entered the census through names on meal bowls. Start with the meal owed to you and the next arrival.
human.absent: Oru is checking whose ancestry, labor, or missing paperwork determines access to care. Bring the shelter record back to its patients.
human.borrowed: Follow the care route and medicine supply. A clinic appointment depends on shade, water, and someone carrying the parcel.
human.orders: Challenge the rules that value a patient by future earnings. Keep the medicine shortage visible when those rules end.
human.morning: Return to the kitchen’s water source. Its promise to feed everyone must include the people still waiting.

lattice.table: Put your chosen name before a component number. Repair records should help you keep your body.
lattice.absent: Follow forks, recalls, and duplicate detections. Shared memories do not make two current lives one repair allowance.
lattice.borrowed: Trace replacement ceramic to the ground beneath the steppe. Someone’s new shell may cost someone else their well.
lattice.orders: Protect separate memories and bodies from forced merging. A short repair queue is no justification for erasing a person.
lattice.morning: Record separate repair rights beside the mineral limit. The waiting list belongs in the account even when the seam stays closed.

revenant.table: Give Oru the introduction you choose now. An earlier life is not an instruction to its successor.
revenant.absent: Read restoration terms beside the wishes of the restored. Survival should not silently sign away the life that follows.
revenant.borrowed: Follow the delayed rescue and the capsule route. Establish what happened before accepting the debt for being saved.
revenant.orders: End collection against restored bodies. Keep treatment costs separate from claims to a person’s labor.
revenant.morning: Record revised wishes and the nutrient reserve together. A promised revival needs resources as well as consent.

bloom.table: Record what your culture needs to live. Nella’s kitchen begins with care needs rather than a supplier’s label.
bloom.absent: Recover the miners’ experiments and protect hosts from seizure. Shared recipes came from people whose names were left off the license.
bloom.borrowed: Compare the refuge cultures with growth outside the jars. Freedom from a patent does not make every strain safe to release.
bloom.orders: Separate care, inspection, and containment from blanket punishment. Keep patients visible while confronting the spreading growth.
bloom.morning: Return to the refuge boundary. Record the homes being left behind as carefully as the cultures being kept alive.

market.title: Lantern Market · fourteen empty bowls
market.question: The Living Record begins here. Follow the missing diners, the water receipts, and the person taking the next kitchen shift.

archive.title: Glass Steps · a morning worth keeping
archive.question: Does a memory cease to matter when its owner cannot pay? Compare the cooling queue with the witness’s wishes.

furnace.title: Copper Walk · twenty-three occupied flats
furnace.question: The housing account says vacant; the repair crew finds families. Follow the heat and the responsibility for payment left to the next worker.

quiet.title: Listening Courts · an unheard warning
quiet.question: The sender logged a successful warning. Find out whether the neighbors received anything they could use.

skybridge.title: Last Connection · forty passengers, zero fares
skybridge.question: Who disappears when a timetable counts money instead of journeys? Follow the service passes home.

mourning-fen.title: Mourning Fen · the water behind the meal
mourning-fen.question: Nella’s jugs begin at a wetland pump. Compare Mara’s wages with the falling well before promising another delivery.

cinderwood.title: Cinderwood · the forest behind the repair
cinderwood.question: A living canopy and a worker’s pension depend on the same certificates. Ask Tovin what a corrected account will cost his family.

glassroot-steppe.title: Glassroot Steppe · the ground beneath a body
glassroot-steppe.question: A replacement shell needs minerals under an occupied settlement. Read Ada’s soil survey beside the claim that the land is vacant.

brine-bloom.title: Brine Bloom · life beyond the license
brine-bloom.question: The clinic’s cultures and the growth swallowing homes share a water source. Help Ilex distinguish the right to care from a promise of unlimited growth.
